title: Consolidate CI artifact staging and selective layer invalidation; roll linter/toolchain upgrades across monorepo
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce CI wall-clock time and flakiness by centralizing artifact staging, implementing selective Docker layer invalidation, and rolling updated linters/toolchains across the monorepo. This ticket covers design, a phased implementation on the ci-runner fleet, cross-team opt-in for risky repositories, and measurement dashboards to validate improvements.
background: Current CI has multiple independent artifact staging patterns: some jobs publish broad tarballs, others echo raw outputs. This leads to redundant uploads and cache churn.

Frequent Docker base image churn invalidates large layers across many services. We can reduce push/pull time by adopting selective invalidation and promoting a tiny stable scratch base for ephemeral builders.
ESLint (frontend) and golangci-lint plus go toolchain are lagging in several packages; dependency drift causes lint CI failures and longer builds for some teams.
Previous tickets (ENG-36501, ENG-40122) improved caching and reduced layer churn but left artifact staging patterns unstandardized across pipelines.
Goal: save 25-40% of median job time for build/test pipelines and eliminate the top sources of cache misses.
Non-goal: full rewrite of all pipelines; we will provide patterns and automation to help teams migrate.
Stakeholders: infra, backend, frontend, platform, and SRE teams.
success_metrics: Median CI build time (pipeline:build-test) reduced by >=30% within 6 weeks of rollout
Artifact upload bandwidth reduced by >=40% for monorepo pipelines
Cache hit rate for base layers increases to >=85% for stable base images
Number of lint-related CI failures reduced by >=70% after staged linter upgrades and autofix migration
implementation_plan: 1) Audit existing pipelines to classify artifact staging patterns (tarball, raw artifacts, container cache blobs). Create standardized templates.
2) Implement a centralized artifact staging service (s3-staging endpoint + manifest) that exposes a small API for jobs to publish and reference artifacts.
3) Introduce selective Docker layer invalidation: split builder images into (stable-base, deps-layer, app-layer). Only rebuild layers when relevant files change using deterministic cache keys.
4) Add cache priming job in nightly window to warm frequently used base layers on all runners/regions.
5) Upgrade ESLint to v9 and update shared config; run autofix pass in a migration branch and provide codemods for teams.
6) Upgrade Go toolchain to 1.21 across services with a dual-toolchain bootstrap in CI (fast-path for older services), and update golangci-lint configs.
7) Provide a gradual opt-in CLI that converts a repo's pipeline to use the new staging templates and selective invalidation; include a dry-run mode.
8) Add dashboards (datadog/grafana) tracking cache hit rates, push/pull sizes, and job latency; wire alerts for regression thresholds.
9) Run canary on 5 low-risk repos, evaluate for 7 days, then schedule a broader rollout with migration office hours.
10) Post-rollout retrospective and cleanup: remove legacy staging paths and update docs.
rollout_plan: Phase A (Canary): 5 non-customer-facing services. Validate cache hit improvement and artifact correctness.
Phase B (Platform): Convert platform and infra repos that depend on the staging service. Provide automation and PR templates.
Phase C (Broader): Open opt-in to all teams with a 4-week migration runway. Offer pairing sessions and codemods for lint autofix.
Fallback: CI will support a feature-flag on the runner side to switch back to legacy staging for a repo if issues are observed.
Cutover completion criteria: 90% of active commits use new staging templates or have an approved migration exemption.
risks_mitigation: Artifact corruption risk: include content-addressed manifests and validation checksums on every publish; verify on fetch.
Cache-thrashing due to incorrect cache keys: start with conservative keys and publish telemetry for key cardinality; roll back if cardinality spikes.
Lint upgrades breaking builds: use a two-week autofix branch and provide a compatibility shim in CI that runs old lint rules for legacy repos during migration.
Toolchain incompatibilities: support dual-toolchain containers for 2 weeks; plan backports where necessary and notify teams with actionable migration steps.
Uploader load on storage: stagger priming jobs and rate-limit staging uploads by repo group to avoid S3 egress spikes.
Operational overhead: provide a one-click migration PR generator and office-hours support to minimize engineering time required per repo.
notes: We intentionally keep the staging API small: publish(manifest) and fetch(manifest). Jobs remain responsible for validating artifact contents.
Consider a short-lived CDN for large base layers in regions with slow egress (APAC), tracked in a follow-up ticket.
SRE recommended starting with 'stable-base:slim' as the canonical base image and only updating it with quarterly cadence unless critical security patches arrive.
We will coordinate with legal for any changes that alter SBOM generation for release artifacts.
